title: Two-Layer Torch Network with Manual Backpropagation
prompt:
Implement `TwoLayerNet` using PyTorch tensor arithmetic: two affine layers with ReLU between them and numerically stable softmax output. Derive and implement backward yourself; do not use `backward`, `torch.autograd`, optimizer helpers, ready-made network layers, or a ready-made loss. Use ordinary tensors with `requires_grad=False` throughout. Tensor arithmetic, ReLU and softmax primitives are allowed.

- `__init__(input_dim, hidden_dim, output_dim, *, dtype=torch.float64, device="cpu")`: initialize weights and biases. Choose your own initialization and internal names. Optional dtype/device select float32/float64 tensors; defaults are float64 on CPU.
- `forward(X)`: return normalized class probabilities `(N, output_dim)` preserving X's dtype/device. X is `(N,input_dim)` with the model's dtype/device; support noncontiguous X.
- `loss(preds,y)`: return scalar Tensor mean cross-entropy from the supplied normalized probabilities and long class-index labels `(N,)`. Use these probabilities directly; do not call forward inside loss or mutate preds. Clamp selected probabilities below `1e-12` only as a loss-reporting guard.
- `train_step(X,y,learning_rate=.1)`: manually compute mean softmax-CE gradients through both affine layers and ReLU, update all parameters using their old values, then return the recomputed loss as a scalar tensor. The probability clamp is a reporting guard; use the usual softmax-CE gradient from logits for training.

Inputs are finite, nonempty, compatible and on the same device, do not require gradients, and labels are valid class indices. Preserve input tensors and singleton dimensions. Learning rate is a Python scalar. This remains a handwritten-backward exercise even though the arrays are Torch tensors.

example.reasoning: A softmax classifier returns one normalized probability row per input example.
